name: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma, mixed cellularity type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic Reed-Sternberg cells in lymph node biopsy
Mixed inflammatory background including eosinophils, plasma cells, histiocytes, and neutrophils
Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD15 and CD30 on Reed-Sternberg cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of Reed-Sternberg cells with typical immunophenotype (CD15+, CD30+) in a mixed inflammatory background on lymph node biopsy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes and reactive conditions is essential

searchTerms: neck lymph node swelling without pain
diagnostic abnormal cells in lymph node biopsy
presence of Reed-Sternberg cells in tissue sample
specific lymphoma cells found on biopsy

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever >38°C, night sweats, weight loss >10%)
searchTerms: fever, night sweats, and weight loss
classic systemic symptoms including fever and sweating
B symptoms like fever and weight loss

common.notes: May cause cough or chest discomfort
Enlarged spleen on physical exam or imaging

occasional.notes: Pain in involved lymph nodes after alcohol intake
searchTerms: lymph node pain triggered by alcohol
pain in lymph nodes after drinking alcohol

rare.notes: Due to mediastinal mass compressing vessels
Very rare in mixed cellularity subtype
searchTerms: nerve problems due to CNS disease

imaging: CT scan revealing lymphadenopathy in cervical, mediastinal, and abdominal regions
genetic: No specific recurrent genetic mutations; clonal rearrangement of immunoglobulin genes may be present
other: Histopathology showing mixed inflammatory infiltrate with Reed-Sternberg cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD15 and CD30, negative for CD45

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrous bands dividing lymph node architecture

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging lymph nodes with systemic symptoms
Unexplained persistent fever and night sweats
Signs of airway obstruction or superior vena cava syndrome
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) Guidelines for Hodgkin Lymphoma, Version 1.2024.
